title: Module 7 Knowledge Check
description: Eight questions on formative and summative evaluation. Unlimited attempts; best score counts.

questions.text: The primary audience for formative evaluation findings is:
options: The design team, to improve the instruction
questions.feedback: Formative evaluation exists to improve instruction before it is finished.

questions.text: In Dick and Carey's sequence, which formative stage is designed to catch gross errors such as wrong content, unclear instructions, and examples that do not work?
questions.feedback: One-to-one evaluation with three learners representing the range of the population finds the gross errors first.

questions.text: A small-group evaluation shows a large overall pre-post gain. What should the designer check before concluding the instruction works?
options: Results by objective, since an overall gain can hide an objective nobody learned
questions.feedback: Analyze item-by-objective. Overall averages hide specific failures.

questions.text: Which are among Kirkpatrick's four levels? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Reaction, learning, behavior, and results. Cost is analyzed in return-on-investment extensions, not as a Kirkpatrick level.

questions.text: High learner satisfaction (level 1) is a reliable indicator that learning (level 2) occurred.
questions.feedback: Satisfaction and learning are only weakly related. Measure learning directly.

questions.text: A help desk saw fewer calls after training was delivered, but a new job aid was released the same week. In a summative evaluation this is an example of:
options: Proof that training caused the reduction
An alternative explanation that the evaluation design must address
questions.feedback: Level 4 outcomes are affected by many factors. Claim contribution, and design for comparisons or baselines that address alternatives.

questions.text: Which formative activity is fastest and finds problems learners cannot name, such as inaccurate content or misaligned assessments?
questions.feedback: Subject-matter, design, and accessibility expert reviews run alongside learner-based stages.

questions.text: What distinguishes a field trial from a small-group evaluation?
options: Field trials occur in the actual setting with the intended facilitators or system and the designer absent, testing implementation
questions.feedback: The field trial tests whether the instruction works under real conditions without the designer present.
